title: Service Lifetimes
description: Learn about different service lifetimes in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: Service lifetime determines when service instances are created and disposed.

data.title: Quick Reference
items: **Transient**: Created each time they are requested.
**Singleton**: Created once for the lifetime of the application.

terms.definition: A lifetime where a new instance is created every time the service is requested.
A lifetime where one instance is created per client request.
A lifetime where one instance is created once and shared across all requests.
A situation where a shorter-lived dependency is held by a longer-lived service, causing unintended behavior.

    C -->|Reused always| C1

data.title: Captive Dependency
data.text: Don't inject a scoped service into a singleton. This causes the scoped service to live as long as the singleton.

data.title: Choose the Right Lifetime
data.description: Decide which lifetime to use for different service types.
steps: Identify whether a service is stateless or stateful
Determine if it holds resources like DbContext
Explain why you chose each lifetime
data.expectedOutcome: Correct lifetime selection with clear reasoning for each choice.

items.hint: Best when the service is stateless and cheap to create.
Ideal for DbContext and business logic services.
Good for caching, configuration, and logging providers.
Never inject Scoped or Transient into a Singleton.

cards.title: Scoped
cards.description: Best for services tied to a single request.
